title: Ab initio atomic structure of matter that exists only once

concept.text: The innovation would determine the atomic arrangement of an unknown, short-lived crystalline phase from one X-ray probe pulse during an irreversible event. The crucial target is a state that cannot be held for static measurement or recreated as equivalent samples for serial measurements. Here, ab initio means solving the structure without a prior atomic model of that phase. A successful measurement would have to contain enough independent structural information to recover the arrangement, rather than merely identify a familiar diffraction pattern.

The intended advance goes beyond the single-pulse structure solutions already demonstrated for simple, highly ordered crystals. It would extend that capability to an unknown transient crystalline phase created by compression, excitation or another irreversible transformation. One such measurement supplies one atomic snapshot. It does not, by itself, provide a time sequence through the unique event, and it does not establish a method for recovering arbitrary atomic configurations in liquids or amorphous matter.

significance.text: Serial crystallography can combine patterns from thousands or millions of similar samples into a structural dataset. Repeatable pump–probe experiments likewise obtain information from equivalent events. Those approaches depend on access to sufficiently equivalent states. A complete structure solution from one pulse would remove that requirement for suitable transient crystals, making phase identity and atomic arrangement experimentally accessible even when the particular state cannot supply a second equivalent measurement.

Conditional significance assessment: the capability could reveal otherwise inaccessible structures during shock compression, extreme excitation or irreversible transformations. Its value depends on the actual target: shock compression and warm dense matter are not inherently non-repeatable, and many experiments in these fields already obtain useful structural information. The revolutionary extension would concern states for which existing static or repeated-event methods cannot deliver an equivalent atomic structure solution.

Downstream synthesis: a directly measured transient structure could constrain interpretations of planetary-interior materials or fusion-relevant matter. Turning that result into a planetary model or an improved fusion design would still require composition, transport properties, thermodynamic information and theory. A structure is a substantial new constraint, not a complete description of the material's behavior or a guaranteed engineering outcome.

The demonstrated Kossel approach also has material restrictions that limit broad impact claims. Its reported route requires at least one heavy element in the unit cell and faces constraints involving crystal quality, sample size, structural complexity and inequivalent fluorescent sites. Extending a successful crystalline snapshot method across extreme matter would therefore require further advances; the existing result does not establish unrestricted coverage of warm dense matter.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is a single-pulse dataset sufficient to solve an unknown transient crystalline structure without pooling structural measurements from other events. With no opportunity to rotate the crystal and collect a conventional sequence of views, the pulse must encode enough independent information. The phase problem must also be resolved: measured scattering strengths alone do not supply all the information needed to reconstruct electron density. The 2024 Kossel demonstration provides a technical basis for addressing both requirements, but its simple-crystal result does not demonstrate the full target.

Preserving usable phase information in realistic transient samples is a concrete barrier. The supplied review of the 2024 supplement reports that mosaic crystals can wash out the Kossel line shapes needed to extract phases. The demonstration used structures with only a few atoms per unit cell; extension to more complicated structures, smaller samples and multiple inequivalent fluorescent sites must overcome additional measurement and interpretation constraints. These are practical obstacles to transferring the method beyond favorable reference crystals.

Scope synthesis: spatial heterogeneity can complicate the interpretation of a transient measurement, but the supplied evidence does not establish the earlier specific attribution to pressure and temperature gradients. Loss of crystalline order is a different issue from insufficient crystal reflections. Liquids and amorphous products require explicitly defined structural observables and inference methods; treating them simply as incomplete crystal datasets would obscure a separate scientific problem.

current_state.text: Bortel and colleagues reported single-pulse structure solutions for GaAs and GaP in Nature Communications on 1 February 2024. Using 25 fs X-ray free-electron-laser pulses, their Kossel measurements yielded structure-factor amplitudes and phases, enabling direct electron-density reconstruction. The samples were large, almost perfect single crystals with simple structures. This is an achieved single-pulse crystallographic result, rather than merely a proposed measurement principle.

Several shots were collected in that experiment, but selected shots were analyzed independently: the reported solutions did not require merging those shots into one structural dataset. This distinction preserves the single-pulse achievement while avoiding the implication that the entire experiment consisted of only one exposure. The reconstructed result also had a chemical-identification limit: Ga and As could not be distinguished within experimental error. Extension to smaller or less perfect crystals was prospective, rather than demonstrated by those samples.

A review by Kraus, Preston and Zastrau, published online on 2 December 2025 and assigned to volume 8, pages 27–39 in 2026, characterized the preceding decade of warm-dense-matter XFEL research as largely consisting of proof-of-principle experiments. The retained abstract and key points describe substantial work on spectroscopy, equations of state, transport, melting and structure. The supplied review had access only to a subscription preview of the main article, so that broad characterization cannot establish the absence of a particular unknown-structure solution.

The supplied assessment of that review's supplement documents single-shot detection of angle-resolved elastic X-ray scattering with large-area detectors, including measurements relevant to liquid-like structure. Such diffraction is an important achieved component. It must be distinguished from recovering a previously unknown crystal structure ab initio: collecting a pattern, measuring correlations, identifying a known phase and solving an unknown atomic arrangement are different accomplishments.

The earlier research attributed dynamic diffraction at terapascal pressures to a Journal of Applied Physics review dated 29 August 2022, citing Lazicki and colleagues in Nature in 2021. No captured text of the AIP review or of the Lazicki paper was available in the supplied evidence. The terapascal component therefore remains unverified within this record; the access gap does not show that the reported result is false.

The supplied evidence establishes the dated 2024 demonstration and the described scope of the 2025 review, but it does not establish whether an unknown extreme transient crystal had been solved from one pulse by 1 November 2026. No freshness assessment was supplied. The reported results are summarized from the provided evidence review; figures, movies and raw data were not visually inspected or independently reanalyzed in that review.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: determine the atomic structure of an unknown transient crystalline phase from one probe pulse during compression, excitation or another irreversible event, without a prior atomic model and without pooling structural data from other shots. The target state should be inaccessible to static measurement and unsuitable for equivalent serial measurements. Repeating the known GaAs demonstration, or indexing one powder ring of a known phase, would not meet this proposed threshold.
completion_criteria.label: Solve unknown transient crystal structure ab initio from one pulse

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evidence package: deposit the solved structure, underlying single-pulse data, analysis procedure and uncertainty estimates before an independent validation experiment. The package should show which structural information came from the pulse, how phases were obtained, which alternative structures remain compatible with the data, and the limits of positional and chemical identification. Independent analysts should be able to reproduce the inference from the deposited measurement.
completion_criteria.label: Deposited single-pulse data enable independent reproduction of structural inference

completion_criteria.text: Proposed physical validation: use a second shot with deliberately changed experimental conditions to test a specified prediction of the deposited structure. That shot should provide an independent check rather than supply missing information needed to solve the original dataset. It need not reproduce an intrinsically unique event exactly; the prediction and the relationship between the two experimental conditions should be stated in advance.
completion_criteria.label: Second-shot validation tests a predeclared structural prediction under changed conditions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: report the demonstrated material class, crystal quality, sample size, structural complexity and chemical discrimination, together with failure conditions. Tests across additional targets would establish the breadth actually demonstrated, not literal universality. A claim extending the capability to liquids or amorphous matter would require a separate definition of the observable and its validation. These criteria are proposals for a convincing demonstration, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Report demonstrated material scope, structural limits and failure conditions

related_concepts.text: Roster-based distinction: CRX-01, Atomic-resolution imaging of a single non-crystalline molecule before destruction, shares the need to obtain sufficient information before the sample is lost. Its target is an individual non-crystalline molecule; CRX-08 concerns an unknown transient crystalline phase. Neither capability implies the other.

Roster-based distinction: CRX-02, Chemically complete atomic structures of bulk amorphous solids, and CRX-04, Atomic ensembles measured from total X-ray scattering, address structural descriptions beyond an ordinary periodic crystal model. Their overlap with CRX-08 becomes relevant if a transient sample loses crystalline order. Amorphous atomic configurations and ensemble or correlation measurements remain distinct targets from solving one transient crystal structure.

Roster-based distinction: CRX-06, Atomic movies of elementary chemical steps without a photo-trigger, seeks a time-resolved account of chemical events. CRX-08 seeks one sufficiently informative structural snapshot during a unique event. Success at the snapshot would not supply a movie or solve the separate problem of observing untriggered chemical steps.

Roster-based editorial boundary: CRX-12, Continuous atomic-resolution crystallography inside working devices and static extreme environments, concerns sustained access to structure in an operating or static environment. CRX-08 concerns information captured during one irreversible event. They may share demanding sample environments and measurement techniques, but continuous observation and a destructive single-event snapshot remain separate goals. This boundary follows the supplied titles and proposed scope; no fuller CRX-12 record was provided.

Roster-based distinction: CRX-03, Chemical-accuracy prediction of which molecular crystal will form, and CRX-07, Predictive experimental selection of a chosen crystal form, concern prediction and control of crystallization. CRX-08 would measure the structure that occurred in a particular transient event. Such a result could inform prediction or selection, but would not itself demonstrate either capability.

Roster-based distinction: CRX-05, Experimental many-electron quantum states of real crystals, and CRX-09, Protonation state as a routine crystallographic observable, seek information beyond basic atomic arrangement. Recovering electron density or atomic positions in CRX-08 would not automatically determine a many-electron quantum state or make protonation assignments routine. The Ga/As discrimination limit in the supplied demonstration illustrates why structural recovery and chemical completeness require separate assessment.

Roster-based distinction: CRX-10, Laboratory sources that do facility-class coherent X-ray crystallography, concerns source capability and access rather than the completeness of a unique-event measurement. CRX-11, Diffraction-quality crystals of arbitrary macromolecules on demand, and CRX-13, A growth rulebook that suppresses defects, twins, and disorder in arbitrary crystals, concern obtaining suitable crystalline samples. Better sources and sample quality could help some implementations of CRX-08, but would not by themselves solve an unknown transient structure or ensure that its state can supply an adequate single-pulse dataset.

change_log.change: Preserved CRX-08 and its original title while defining the immediate technical target as an unknown transient crystalline structure.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports a crystallographic capability; it does not establish recovery of arbitrary atomic configurations across all forms of matter.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical statements that unknown one-shot extreme-matter structures remain unsolved with a dated account and an explicit freshness limitation.
change_log.reason: The supplied record does not establish continued non-achievement through 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Retained the 25 fs GaAs/GaP result and added independent shot analysis, simple-crystal scope and the Ga/As discrimination limit.
change_log.reason: These details preserve the achieved single-pulse result while making its experimental and chemical limits clear.

change_log.change: Added the Kossel route's heavy-element requirement, sensitivity to mosaicity and restrictions involving sample size, complexity and fluorescent sites.
change_log.reason: The review identifies concrete barriers to extending the demonstrated method beyond favorable crystals.

change_log.change: Separated liquid and amorphous structural observables from incomplete crystalline diffraction, and qualified the pressure/temperature-gradient explanation.
change_log.reason: Noncrystalline structure requires a different formulation, and the specific gradient mechanism was not substantiated by the supplied evidence.

change_log.change: Separated single-shot diffraction, phase identification and correlation measurements from ab initio solution of an unknown crystal.
change_log.reason: These achievements provide different levels and kinds of structural information.

change_log.change: Preserved the warm-dense-matter review's characterization while recording partial main-article access and substantial achieved diffraction capability.
change_log.reason: Broad proof-of-principle language does not establish the absence of the proposed specific breakthrough.

change_log.change: Qualified the terapascal diffraction assertion rather than presenting it as verified or deleting it.
change_log.reason: Neither the cited AIP review text nor the Lazicki paper was supplied; missing evidence does not refute the assertion.

change_log.change: Recast the second validation shot as a test of a specified structural prediction, with prior deposition of the original inference.
change_log.reason: Exact repetition conflicts with an intrinsically unique event; independent validation need not recreate that event.

change_log.change: Made deposition, reproducibility and practical boundaries explicit proposed criteria, without inventing numerical standards.
change_log.reason: The candidate supplied a proposed demonstration, not an established community benchmark.

change_log.change: Removed the unverifiable historical-item attribution and expanded distinctions across the supplied concept roster.
change_log.reason: No historical benchmark text was provided, and roster relationships should clarify overlap without merging entries.

unresolved_issues: Whether an unknown transient crystalline structure meeting the proposed single-pulse criteria had been demonstrated by 1 November 2026 remains unresolved; no freshness assessment was supplied.
The terapascal dynamic-diffraction assertion remains unverified within the supplied record because the cited AIP review and Lazicki paper were not available as evidence.
The supplied material does not quantify how far the demonstrated Kossel method can extend in sample size, disorder, structural complexity or inequivalent fluorescent sites.
The specific role of pressure and temperature gradients in preventing a sufficient dataset was not established by the supplied evidence.
No validated noncrystalline observable or completion criterion was supplied for extending this concept to liquids or amorphous matter.
A concrete target and a feasible independent prediction for the deliberately different validation shot remain to be specified.
The historical item 9 comparison cannot be assessed without its text; relationships to other roster entries are limited to their supplied titles and the stated CRX-08 scope.
